CIEL: Please forgive me.
I'm afraid I'm not fit to perform at the moment.
Not on a stage,
Nor face to face,
Nor anywhere else.
I may act like a star, but it is just that, after all.
No matter how clean the makeup is, I know I'm just a country girl in over her head.
Often literally.
I grew up in a farm town where the most exciting thing was watching the clouds pass.
I didn't have much in the way of friends, nor avenues with which to meet them.
Just a family that was fractured in exactly as mundane a way as anyone else's.
It was somewhere between drab and vexatious.
One day, a traveling circus came to the nearby city.
My cousin and I snuck away to meet it, and just--
The lights--
The sounds--
Complete sensory overload.
I was sick for a week.
But the people were fantastic.
The stars were all good and well, but the audience--
THEY were something.
Everyone from bleacher to bleacher couldn't help but smile and cheer.
I felt more love in that little tent than I had in most of my life.
And I was sure that such amazing performers could never be bored, or lonely.
If I could just be like them--
But no.
I never could.
I am just a bumpkin flailing in the silks.
I don't have half of their talent, grace, or beauty.
My knees are too stubby, my shoulders too broad, and good graces, have you SEEN my dimples?
How anyone finds the strength to put palm to palm is beyond me.
I am sure it is an act of charity, if not mockery.
My own carelessness pushed my kin away, sights set on stars too high.
And even so--
The others never minded.
Samson had always looked out for me, no matter how much I rejected his advances.
And Terra-- obnoxious as she was--
They didn't think about whether I was real or not.
They were just there.
Brutish and clamorous and altogether the picture of indecency...
But I do have such fond memories...
And now they're gone.
Pack it up; the show is over.
Better go back to watching the clouds.
That one looks like a star.
Perhaps I could ask for its autograph.
CIEL: I thought stardom might bring me closer to others.
It turns out that admiration is just another form of distance.
